question: A writer wants Claude to draft technical explanations as flowing prose paragraphs rather than bullet-heavy markdown. Which instruction best achieves this for a drafting task?
options: A) Ask Claude to bullet every key point so the explanation is easy to scan
B) Tell Claude to write flowing prose, reserving markdown for code and simple headings
C) Tell Claude not to use any markdown, without saying what the response should look like
D) Leave the formatting instructions out and hope the default style matches
correct_answers: B) Tell Claude to write flowing prose, reserving markdown for code and simple headings
explanations: Incorrect. Requesting bullets for every point produces the opposite of the flowing prose paragraphs the writer is asking for.
Correct. Telling Claude what to do instead of what not to do, describing the desired prose style directly, is the more effective way to steer output formatting for long-form drafting.
Incorrect. A bare prohibition without describing the desired prose format is a less effective way to steer formatting than telling Claude what to produce instead.
Incorrect. Omitting formatting guidance leaves the output style to chance rather than steering it toward the flowing prose the writer wants.
